description: Frozen regression protocol: how a pretrained encoder is turned into an energy regressor per dataset and label regime.

modes.probe: encoder frozen (eval mode, embeddings computed once and cached); only the regression head trains
modes.full: encoder and head train (lower learning rate for the encoder)
modes.scratch: same encoder architecture with random weights, same recipe (the control)

head: pooled embedding (masked mean over tokens, or the event embedding) -> LayerNorm(D); log E = c[detector] + a * log_scale + MLP([LayerNorm(emb), standardised log_scale, detector embedding(8)]); MLP = Linear(D + 9, 128) -> GELU -> Linear(128, 1) with a zero-initialised last layer; c and a are trainable and start at the least-squares calibration of log E on log_scale (per detector for MJD) over the labeled events, so training starts from the amplitude calibration
target: log of the reference energy (keV); training events with reference energy <= 1 keV are skipped (log undefined); predictions are exp(log E)
loss: Huber(delta = 1) on (log E_pred - log E_ref) / 0.01 (1 % relative error = 1 unit)

schedule.decay: cosine to zero over the planned steps

early_stopping.metric: mean loss on the selection subset

selection_subset.note: positions = sorted first N of default_rng(seed).permutation(n_validation); energies used for selection only, never for gradients

data_loading: labeled inputs held in memory when they fit NLDBD_FINETUNE_RAM_GB (default 8), else streamed through the regression view each pass in file order and shuffled inside a buffer of 8192 events
